context: The integer n is positive. The following count assumes execution without tail-call optimization.

frames.explanation: In the left column, “Descend,” the argument decreases by 1 at each call, from linear_recur(n) down to the base case linear_recur(1). A brace is labeled “Recursion depth n.” Each outer call waits for its child, so n frames coexist at the deepest point. The right column, “Unwind,” shows the calls returning one at a time. Each frame is released only when its call returns. The figure shows return 0, while the current Python code uses a bare return and returns None. This difference does not affect the stack space count.
frames.title: Stack space used by recursive calls

result: Each level uses constant local space. At maximum depth, n levels are active at once, so peak stack space is O(n). Releasing frames afterward does not change the peak already reached.
summary: Stack space depends on how many calls are active at once. Each deeper call adds a stack frame.
title: Stack space used by recursive calls
